advice: Experiment: test a 2VL×2VL SME output tile with column-major ZA stores to a temporary contiguous C tile, then copy each tile row to row-major C with contiguous scalar/vector stores. Keep the existing full A transpose, FP32 MOPA selectors 0–3, reduction order, tile coverage, and general predicated tail path. This isolates whether ZA vertical stores plus a row copy improve output-store efficiency; all scratch allocation and copying stay inside gemm. Do not assume alignment: malloc aligns the scratch base, but tile row starts are separated by the active tile width and may not meet any stronger alignment requirement. Use unaligned-safe stores unless each address is proven aligned.
risks: The extra copy and scratch traffic may cost more than the existing direct horizontal ZA stores. The change must preserve every output exactly within the fixed 0.002 relative max-error limit, including odd tails and n<=0. It is a hypothesis only; assess it with the unchanged correctness checks and fresh serial AC controls. The supplied history contains no evidence that this store layout is faster.
